summary.text: 人 is a pictograph of a person standing in profile. Early examples are used for ‘person’; the familiar form is a greatly simplified-looking continuation of that figure, not a combination of separate modern components. [ref013][ref014][ref020][ref021]

formation.text: Pictographic: the whole graph depicts a standing person in profile. Paleographic descriptions interpret the figure as a head, body, arm and legs; this is an interpretation of the image, not a demonstrated stroke-by-stroke sequence. [ref013][ref014][ref021]

history.text: The dossier records oracle-bone and bronze forms, followed by Small Seal material. Its selected oracle-style and seal-script illustrations are modern redrawings; they show examples of those script traditions and do not establish a direct evolutionary sequence. [ref014][ref015][ref024][ref026][ref028]

The account in Shuowen describes 人 as depicting an arm and shin. This is a historical explanation, while modern paleographic descriptions support reading the graph as a profile figure. Some shapes called ancient in later references are not attested in the early corpora checked, so they should not be assumed to be ancestors. [ref003][ref016][ref021][ref029]

uncertainties.text: The cited oracle-bone examples are assigned to that script tradition, but their individual dates and the character’s first-use date are not supplied. The evidence supports ‘person’ as an early meaning without establishing a more precise origin date. [ref013][ref015][ref020]

The dossier reports instances where 人 was used to write other graphs or words, including 夷 and 年, but does not independently establish the sound correspondences behind those whole-graph loans. It also reports 人 as a phonetic element within 年; these are distinct claims. [ref013][ref019][ref022]

senses.period: Oracle-bone inscriptions; individual specimen dates unresolved
senses.text: The graph is interpreted as depicting a person, and cited oracle-bone examples use it in contexts glossed ‘ten people’ and ‘I, the king’. The sources do not date the individual specimens. [ref013][ref020]
Bronze-inscription examples are reported with uses glossed ‘common people’ and ‘people’. Their exact dates and priority relative to one another are not given. [ref013]

senses.gloss: the speaker or ruler referring to himself
senses.period: Oracle-bone inscriptions; individual specimen date unresolved
senses.text: One cited oracle-bone example is interpreted as a ruler’s self-reference. The evidence records this use but does not establish how it developed from ‘person’. [ref013][ref020]
The supplied character glosses include ‘someone else’ and ‘other person’, but do not provide a dated history for this sense. [ref007][ref009]

limitations.text: The evidence gives early ‘person’ uses and selected later glosses, but not a complete dated account of how the senses ‘person’, ‘people’, self-reference, and ‘someone else’ relate. No semantic path between them is asserted. [ref013][ref015]

The reports of 人 used for 夷 or 年 concern writing another word with this graph. The available evidence does not supply independently established sound comparisons, so these are not presented as demonstrated phonetic loans or as semantic developments. [ref019][ref022]

overview.text: 人 is a picture of a person seen from the side. Early examples use it for ‘person’; the graph does not need to be split into smaller parts to explain it. [ref013][ref014][ref020]
